sources.fact: Current authoritative Brownfield entity is LBBD17/BO, Elim Pentecostal Church, 194 Ripple Road, Barking.
The record gives 9 minimum and maximum net dwellings on 0.06ha.
The structured fields say permissioned with full-planning-permission dated 9 February 2016.
The same current record carries the note Lapsed; the structured status and note are retained as a conflict requiring current-case reconciliation.
Ownership-status is not-owned-by-a-public-authority and is not a named proprietor/title relation.
The record supplies a point and blank geometry rather than exact application or HMLR polygons.
Planning Data links the record to planning-history id 14160.
The 8 February 2016 Committee considered 15/01099/FUL for demolition of the church and a replacement church with 4 one-bedroom and 5 two-bedroom flats above.
The Board granted permission subject to conditions, including a three-year commencement limit.
The historic grant is not treated as currently implementable because the authoritative current record explicitly notes Lapsed.
194 Ripple Road is not merged with the former Westbury Arms site at 174-176 Ripple Road despite equal nine-home capacity.
No replacement application, lawful commencement proof, current title topology or executed statutory overlay bundle was verified this wave.

examples.result: BO retains a nine-home historic full-permission record.
The current Lapsed note is preserved and blocks current-permission inference.
The 2016 Committee grant is not represented as an active 2026 consent.
The replacement church use does not create additional dwelling capacity.
BO is not merged with BZ merely because both are on Ripple Road and each has nine homes.
The Brownfield point is not converted into title geometry.
Non-public ownership category is not named proprietor evidence.
Promotion remains zero until a current replacement case, title relation and overlays are verified.
